newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MINISTERS SEEK MORE FUNDS TO FIGHT S.AFRICAN CRIME.
newsitem.headline: MINISTERS SEEK MORE FUNDS TO FIGHT S.AFRICAN CRIME.

text.p: The three ministers in charge of South Africa's criminal justice system plan an urgent joint appeal to Treasury for enough funds to implement a major drive against soaring crime.
Justice Minister Dullah Omar told a media briefing that the move by himself, Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi and Correctional Services Minister Sipho Mzimela was unprecedented.

"For the first time, the idea is that we will together go to Treasury to discuss the funds which we require to ensure the effective implementation of the national crime prevention strategy (NCPS)," Omar said.
Historically, each department meets Treasury on its own to talk about its own needs.
Omar said he was aware of the need for fiscal discipline but said that government must regard the fight against crime as a top priority.
Rising crime, including vehicle hijackings and drug dealing, have been blamed for growing business pessimism, high emigration rates and a growing violent death toll in South Africa.

Police figures show South Africa is one of the world's most crime-ridden societies. A total of 1.98 million serious crimes were reported last year, with only half solved, including 36,888 rapes, 18,983 murders and 66,838 armed robberies.
"Now that we have a national crime prevention strategy in place, the necessary funding must be provided to ensure that it is implemented completely and fully," Omar said.
"The strategy is a very good strategy. It does provide South Africa with its first ever national crime prevention strategy. We can draw in all the role players. We can draw in communities.
"We can ensure that there is an effective fight against crime but we must make sure that the necessary funding is there for that particular purpose."

Parliamentary justice committee chairman Johnny de Lange told the briefing that the criminal justice system needed easy access to quick funds to deal with emergencies rather than being locked into the current budgetary cycle.
"That is why one of the matters that we are looking at is to have a dedicated fund for the NCPS, which one can access quite easily, obviously with all the checks and balances," De Lange said.
